english.title: Receiving benefit from participant in unfair trading scheme
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were a person to whom or for whose benefit a payment was made by a

(A)_[participant]_
(B)_[person who had applied or been invited to become a participant]_

in a trading scheme to which Part XI of the Fair Trading Act 1973 Act applied who had made a payment to or for the benefit of the promoter or (if there is more than one) any of the promoters, or to or for the benefit of a participant in the trading scheme, having been induced to make that payment by reason that the prospect was held out to

(C)_[him]_
(D)_[her]_

of receiving payments or other benefits in respect of the introduction of other persons who became participants in the trading scheme
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 120(3) and 122 of the Fair Trading Act 1973.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the prescribed sum.

Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see section 129 of the Fair Trading Act 1973

Note
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
